title: Side Chapter · Gear and Protection
subtitle: Lenses and suits against MRU, then tools

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:magic_monocle}
items: essentialcraft5:magic_monocle

blocks.text: A cluster is most dangerous behind a wall or under the floor. By the time you notice it, it has usually filled. First make a lens that sees through walls, then clothes that keep it out.

This chapter covers what you carry and wear, starting with gear that shows MRU and keeps it out, then better tools. Every page is optional, so make what you need. The monocle, the Tier 2 wand and MHS armor only need the alloys from Chapter 6. The [[gear/elemental_tools|weakened elemental tools]] come earlier still and need nothing past Chapter 1. The later pages each say when you can start them.
Goal (optional): make a {item:essentialcraft5:magic_monocle} so you can see nearby MRUCUs through walls. An MRUCU is a ball of MRU hanging in the air, usually leaked by machines ([[start/mrucu]]).

MRUCUs can always be seen, but the ones inside walls or underground are easy to miss. By the time you notice one, it may already hold 10,000 MRU and be [[corruption/matrix_damage|damaging your matrix]].
You need: three {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_gold_alloy}s and one {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_glass_alloy}, both cheap to make on the Magician Table ([[alloys/purified_alloys]]).
How to use it

items: Hold it in either hand and nearby MRUCUs show up through blocks.
Right-click to put it on, or place it in the helmet slot. On your head it works the same and leaves both hands free, but it takes the place of a helmet.
Worn or held, it also shows the MRU particles that permanent magic lights give off ([[essence/magical_lantern]]).
It has no durability and never breaks.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have a monocle. Hold or wear it, and MRUCUs behind walls come into view.
Going further: holding the [[gear/mru_mover_t2]], or wearing the helmet of the [[gear/mhs_armor]] or a later armor set, also shows MRUCUs through walls.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:mru_mover_t2}
items: essentialcraft5:mru_mover_t2

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make an {item:essentialcraft5:mru_mover_t2}. It works just like the first {item:essentialcraft5:mru_mover} ([[crafting/corruption]]), and while held it also shows MRUCUs through walls the way the monocle does, so one wand both finds them and moves them.

You need: two {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_glass_alloy}s, one diamond and two {item:essentialcraft5:magical_ingot}s. From Chapter 12 on, a {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem} can replace the diamond. The ingots are the Magician Table kind from Chapter 3 ([[crafting/magician_crafts]]), not the {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_gold_alloy} the monocle uses.
How to use it

items: Aim at an MRUCU and hold right-click to pull it toward you. Sneak to push it away instead.
It reaches about 20 blocks ahead and moves the MRUCU 2 blocks per second.
Move big MRUCUs off to a corner, away from where you spend your time.

rows: 1,536, lost at 1 per second only while it is actually moving something, about 25 minutes in all

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have the wand. Hold it and you can both see MRUCUs behind walls and pull them over.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The wand only moves an MRUCU when both the space it is in and the space it is moving into are places you are allowed to change. Ones inside someone else's claim or in the protected area around spawn won't budge, and nothing can be moved past the world border. The first wand has the same limits.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:mrucu_container}
items: essentialcraft5:mrucu_container

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make an {item:essentialcraft5:mrucu_container}. A mover can only drag an MRUCU along a little at a time. This flask takes in the whole MRUCU, MRU and all, so you can carry it somewhere else and let it out.

You need: two {item:essentialcraft5:magical_ingot}s, three {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_glass_alloy}s and a diamond. From Chapter 12 on, a {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem} can replace the diamond. The materials are close to those of the [[gear/mru_mover_t2]], so if you can make that wand you can make this.
How to use it

items: Point an empty flask at an MRUCU within 6 blocks and hold right-click for about 2 seconds. Purple sparks appear between the MRUCU and the neck of the flask, and you have to keep looking at the MRUCU the whole time or it won't go in.

Capturing costs {cfg:general.mrucu_container.capture_cost_percent|pctv} of the MRUCU's stored MRU, taken first from the [[storage/soul_storage|soul storage]] you carry. If you can't pay, it stays where it is.
With a full flask, right-click a block. The MRUCU appears in the middle of the space just outside the face you clicked, and the flask is empty again. Letting it out costs no MRU.

rows: Hold right-click for 2 seconds and pay {cfg:general.mrucu_container.capture_cost_percent|pctv} of its stored MRU
One MRUCU, with its MRU and balance unchanged

blocks.text: Sealed in the flask, the MRUCU hurts no one, takes in no leaked MRU and merges with no other MRUCU. The swirl of light inside changes color with its balance, and the tooltip shows how much MRU it holds. The flask itself is fireproof, so dropping it in lava won't destroy the MRUCU along with it.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have a flask. Hold right-click on an MRUCU and the whole thing goes into the flask.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: You can only capture and release where you are allowed to build, judged by the MRUCU's space when capturing and by the target space when releasing. The release spot must also be inside the world border and outside spawn protection. MRUCUs on someone else's claim can't be taken, and yours can't be let out on theirs.

In the original mod an MRUCU counted as a creature, and players often carried whole ones off with mob-catching tools. Since the port it is no longer a creature and those tools don't recognize it, which is why this flask exists.

entries.title: MHS Armor
items: essentialcraft5:mhs_helmet
essentialcraft5:mhs_chestplate
essentialcraft5:mhs_leggings
essentialcraft5:mhs_boots

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make a full set of MHS (Magical Hazmat Suit) armor, which is the {item:essentialcraft5:mhs_helmet}, {item:essentialcraft5:mhs_chestplate}, {item:essentialcraft5:mhs_leggings} and {item:essentialcraft5:mhs_boots}. It is the first gear that keeps MRU off you. MRU Corruption hurts less while you wear it, and big MRUCUs can barely touch your matrix. While charged, it also takes part of the hits you take.

The forebears put on a suit like this before going near the cages that held MRUCUs. Standing by leaking machines keeps stacking the MRU Corruption effect, and MRUCUs holding 10,000 MRU or more damage the matrix of players around them ([[crafting/corruption]]). If you spend a lot of time at your machines, make yourself a set.
Prepare

The full set takes eight {item:essentialcraft5:combined_magical_alloys}, five {item:essentialcraft5:world_interactor}s, twelve {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plate}s, one {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_glass_alloy} and ten {item:essentialcraft5:crystal_dust}, about 140,000 MRU in all.

The alloys are the big cost. Eight of them need 64 {item:minecraft:blaze_powder} and 64 {item:minecraft:ender_pearl}s ([[alloys/combined_magical_alloys]]). Farm the blaze powder at a Nether fortress first, then hunt endermen at night.

items: essentialcraft5:mhs_helmet
essentialcraft5:mhs_chestplate
essentialcraft5:mhs_leggings
essentialcraft5:mhs_boots

blocks.text: Armor

rows: +{cfg:general.mhs_armor.max_health} per piece, {cfg:general.mhs_armor.max_health|mul:4} for the set ({cfg:general.mhs_armor.max_health|mul:2} hearts)

blocks.text: Mending is the easiest way to repair it. You can also combine two pieces at an anvil (the right-hand one is used up), but no material repairs it there, and a crafting grid or grindstone won't combine it. The [[devices/magical_repairer]] can fix it at a steep MRU price, {cfg:machines.magical_repairer.mru_usage|mul:1536} MRU to bring a chestplate up from 0.
Matrix Buffer

Each piece holds <t>{cfg:general.mhs_armor.max_mru|at:0} MRU</t>, and fills up in a [[storage/charging_chamber]]. When you take physical damage such as a melee hit or a projectile, or elemental damage such as fire, lava, an explosion or lightning, every charged piece blocks its own share: helmet {cfg:general.mhs_armor.shares_helmet|at:0}/20, chestplate {cfg:general.mhs_armor.shares_chestplate|at:0}/20, leggings {cfg:general.mhs_armor.shares_leggings|at:0}/20, boots {cfg:general.mhs_armor.shares_boots|at:0}/20.

Each piece pays for every block, <t>{cfg:general.mhs_armor.mru_per_damage} MRU</t> per point of its share, rounded down and never less than 1 point. If the storage items you carry, such as a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard}, can cover it between them, they pay; otherwise the whole amount comes out of the piece itself.
From matrix rank 2, when your soul storage runs short the cost comes from your [[matrix/reservoir|Matrix Reservoir]] next, and only then from the piece's own charge.

cells: every piece counts as 1 point, 400 MRU for the set, blocking 2
helmet 100 + chestplate 200 + leggings 100 + boots 100 = 500 MRU, blocking 5; the chestplate's own charge covers 10 such hits

blocks.text: Fully charged, a 20-point hit costs you only 5.25 health in this set, against 8 in diamond and 7.2 in netherite. Without charge it holds up just like diamond.
Magic and falling aren't blocked, and neither is damage that ignores armor, such as burning after you catch fire or freezing.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: <w>A piece with no charge of its own doesn't block</w>, and won't draw on your storage items. A piece that can't pay doesn't block that hit either, and you take its share.
While you wear it, a small box left of the hotbar shows how much charge your MRU-shielded armor has left in all. The tooltip also says roughly how many 20-point hits the piece can block when full.
Attunement stages enlarge both the share and each piece's charge ([[attunement/mhs_armor]]).
MRU resistance
Each piece carries a few resistances, listed in its tooltip. They only count while worn in an armor slot, not in your inventory.

rows: 12.5%; nothing in this mod causes it, so you can ignore it

blocks.text: What gets through = 1 − (sum of the four pieces) ÷ 4

With the full set, 0.75 gets through, so each MRU Corruption hit drops from {cfg:general.corruption.mru_corruption_health_percent|pct} to {cfg:general.corruption.mru_corruption_health_percent|mul:0.75|pct} of your max health.
[[hoanna/radiation]] is worked out the same way. With the full set, each second's gain is multiplied by <t>0.9</t> and rounded down, which comes to about 1 point less per second.
Against MRUCUs

An MRUCU holding 10,000 MRU or more adds matrix damage to players within 12 blocks once a second. Each full 10,000 MRU counts as one tier, so a full 20,000 is tier 2. Damage follows the formula below, and with no protection "what gets through" counts as 0.99.
Matrix damage per second = ⌊4 × tier ÷ (10 − 10 × what gets through)⌋

A single piece already cuts 40 down to 6, so even the helmet alone is worth making first. Blocks in between lower the odds further. Behind {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone} only one second in two counts, and behind {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_glass} only one in three.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off once you have had all four pieces. The helmet, while worn, shows MRUCUs through walls just like the monocle.
Going further: once you have been to Hoanna, you can upgrade it into [[gear/void_armor]].

entries.title: Void Armor
entries.summary: While charged, melee and arrows cannot touch you
items: essentialcraft5:void_helmet
essentialcraft5:void_chestplate
essentialcraft5:void_leggings
essentialcraft5:void_boots

blocks.text: Goal (optional): upgrade your MHS armor into Void Armor, which is the {item:essentialcraft5:void_helmet}, {item:essentialcraft5:void_chestplate}, {item:essentialcraft5:void_leggings} and {item:essentialcraft5:void_boots}. It has high armor values, and the full set adds {cfg:general.void_armor.max_health|mul:4} max health. While it holds MRU, melee hits and arrows can't touch you.
Prepare

The full set takes four [[gear/mhs_armor|MHS pieces]], seven {item:minecraft:nether_star}s, five {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor}s, eight {item:essentialcraft5:void_core}s, eight {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating}s and four {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity}. Matter of Eternity is a big battery made from a Nether Star ([[storage/soul_storage]]).
Each Matter of Eternity takes another Nether Star, so the set costs 11 Nether Stars in all. Start saving them early.

Void Cores and MRU Reactors come from the [[hoanna/relics|relic chests]] the people of Hoanna left behind, about 0.2 of each per chest, so eight Void Cores mean opening some 40 chests. Open every chest you find there. Defeated [[hologram/hologram|Holographic Projections]] drop a few as well. <w>The later main-line chapters still need about 15 cores and 12 reactors</w>, so set those aside first ([[hoanna/relics]]).

If you run short of chests, an MRUCU shut in an Enrichment Chamber in Hoanna can [[hoanna/collapse|collapse]] instead, giving 1 every {cfg:machines.enrichment_chamber.collapse.seconds|div:60|round:1} minutes.
Once you have defeated a Holographic Projection, the [[ley/ley_condenser]] can slowly make Nether Stars, so there's no need to hunt wither skeletons.

items: essentialcraft5:void_helmet
essentialcraft5:void_chestplate
essentialcraft5:void_leggings
essentialcraft5:void_boots

blocks.text: Each recipe has the MHS piece for the same slot in the middle of the second row, and uses it up. The chestplate's top row is two reactors around a Nether Star; the other three have two Nether Stars around a reactor.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: <w>The MRU stored in the Matter of Eternity is used up with it</w>, so drain it first. Enchantments on the MHS piece don't carry over either.
Armor
These stats apply whether or not the armor holds MRU. If the set adds up to more than the game allows, the excess doesn't count; the caps are <t>30</t> armor and <t>20</t> toughness.
Charged: blocks physical damage

Each piece holds <t>{cfg:general.void_armor.max_mru} MRU</t>, shown in its tooltip, and fills up in a [[storage/charging_chamber]]. When you take a melee hit, or are struck by an arrow, trident or other projectile, every charged piece blocks its own share of the damage: helmet 3/20, chestplate 8/20, leggings 6/20, boots 3/20.
With all four charged, the whole hit is blocked and you lose no health, though the knockback still happens.

Each piece pays MRU for every block, <t>{cfg:general.void_armor.mru_per_damage} MRU</t> per point of its share, rounded down and never less than 1 point. If the storage items you carry, such as a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard}, can cover it between them, they pay. Otherwise the whole amount comes out of the piece itself.
Storage items worn in the accessory bar don't count while a [[computer/seal_field|Curio Seal Field]] seals them. Storage anywhere else on you still does.

rows: every piece counts as 1 point, 1,600 MRU for the set
helmet 400 + chestplate 1,200 + leggings 800 + boots 400 = 2,800 MRU; the chestplate's own charge covers 41 such hits
helmet 1,200 + chestplate 3,200 + leggings 2,400 + boots 1,200 = 8,000 MRU; the chestplate's own charge covers 15 such hits

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: <w>A piece that can't pay doesn't block that hit</w>, and you take its share. A piece with no MRU of its own doesn't block at all, and won't draw on your storage items. Before a big fight, charge all four pieces and carry a few storage items.

With the {item:essentialcraft5:eta_amulet} on, a hit of 8 becomes 16, but the shield ignores the extra 8 it adds: that part goes straight to your armor and health, and the shield only blocks and charges for the original 8.
While you carry the {item:essentialcraft5:infinite_mru_crystal}, it pays all of this. As long as each piece holds a little charge of its own, Void Armor and the [[computer/suit]] keep blocking.

It only blocks physical damage. Fire, lava, explosions, lightning, freezing, magic, thorns, falling and drowning cost no MRU and are reduced by the armor values above as usual. Damage that ignores armor isn't blocked either.
From attunement stage 3 it blocks elemental damage too ([[attunement/void_armor]]).
What each piece does

rows: Killing a creature other than a player restores hunger equal to its max health ÷ 10 (2 for a zombie, one drumstick). Also shows MRUCUs through walls
A <t>{cfg:general.gear_growth.void_armor.dodge|stage:0|pct}</t> chance to dodge any damage except falling out of the world and /kill, losing no health and spending no MRU
Fall damage is cut to a tenth; you walk much faster and step straight up full blocks

blocks.text: Full set: Void Riposte and calamity protection

With all four on, for 3 seconds after the chestplate dodges a hit from a creature, your next solid melee hit deals 50% more damage, or {cfg:general.attunement.pvp_effect_scale|mul:0.5|pct} more against a player.
With all four on, the Sun Array's burning, an earthquake's push and the poison from Poison Fumes in Hoanna's [[hoanna/events|calamities]] are halved.
Attunement stages strengthen the dodge, the riposte and this protection from calamities ([[attunement/void_armor]]).
MRU resistance
Each piece carries resistances that only count in an armor slot. Like the other stats, they don't depend on how much MRU the piece holds.
With the full set, MRU Corruption can't hurt you at all, and big MRUCUs can no longer add to your matrix damage.

With the full set, the [[hoanna/radiation]] a chunk gives you each second is cut to a quarter, rounded down. Outside the Dreadlands that never beats the 1 point that fades each second, so it stops rising however long you stay. In the Dreadlands it rises by at most 1 per second.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have any piece of Void Armor.
Fine print

Taking it off removes the extra max health, and your health drops with it. Logging out and back in, or coming back from the End, leaves your health as it was. If you respawn with the set on after dying, you start at 20 health and regenerate the rest.
The original research book called it "the best armor in the game", and the leggings' description promised they could "phase-shift through monsters". The original never made that work.

blocks.text: Goal (optional): switch to elemental tools. They come in two sets. The {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_pickaxe} set is made of {item:essentialcraft5:mru_resonating_crystal} and beats netherite. The {item:essentialcraft5:weak_elemental_pickaxe} set is made of {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_drops_block}, matches diamond and costs far less.

A pickaxe or axe takes 3 of its material, a hoe or sword 2, a shovel 1. An {item:essentialcraft5:mru_resonating_crystal} is made in the Radiating Chamber from one diamond and one emerald, at 5,000 MRU each. One {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_drops_block} is crafted from nine {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_gem}s.

From Matrix Rank 3 the {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_sword} carries a [[matrix/alignment|Matrix Trait]]: every hit that lands adds one more effect based on your matrix type. The weakened sword doesn't.

blocks.title: Saving diamonds
blocks.text: When diamonds are scarce, a resonating crystal can take {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem}s in place of both the diamond and the emerald. One diamond turns into four pale gems, enough for two crystals. You can only make [[gear/pale_gem]]s once you have Pale Blocks from Chapter 12.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have any one of them.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Keep a few spare. The elemental pickaxe goes into the [[gear/magical_digger]], the elemental sword into the {item:essentialcraft5:chaos_fork}, {item:essentialcraft5:frozen_mace}, {item:essentialcraft5:holy_mace} and {item:essentialcraft5:spiky_shield}, and the elemental hoe into the {item:essentialcraft5:staff_of_life}. Their enchantments are lost in the recipe.

Mending is the easiest way to repair them, and combining two works too, but no material repairs them on an anvil. The [[devices/magical_repairer]] can fix them as well, though it burns through MRU: {cfg:machines.magical_repairer.mru_usage|mul:3568} MRU to bring an elemental pickaxe up from 0.
Going further: the [[wind_gear/wind_tools]] switch between five forms in a single item, with more durability and a higher tier. They are made from [[wind/wind_gem]].

Goal (optional, and only worth it if you plan to make a {item:essentialcraft5:chaos_fork} or a {item:essentialcraft5:frozen_mace}): absorb a matrix projection to change the nature of your own MRU matrix.
Goal (optional, though matrix rank 3 needs a type other than Neutral, so you will want to do it once before Chapter 10): absorb a matrix projection to change the nature of your own MRU matrix.

Few of the forebears ever did this, and the absorbing is not pleasant. The [[generators/projections|matrix projections]] you make in the Radiating Chamber are more than ingredients. Absorb one and your matrix takes on its nature: a {item:essentialcraft5:chaos_matrix_projection} makes it chaotic, a {item:essentialcraft5:frozen_matrix_projection} frozen, a {item:essentialcraft5:magic_matrix_projection} magical, a {item:essentialcraft5:shade_matrix_projection} shadowy, and an {item:essentialcraft5:empty_matrix_projection} turns it back to neutral.

A matrix's nature has no passive effect at all and only matters for weapons. A chaos matrix goes with the {item:essentialcraft5:chaos_fork} and a frozen one with the {item:essentialcraft5:frozen_mace}, and their hits only carry special effects when the matrix matches ([[staffs/matrix_weapons]]). Magic, shade and neutral matrices have no matching weapon. If you don't plan to use those two, absorbing a projection brings nothing but the cost.

From matrix rank 3, your matrix type gives you a passive called [[matrix/alignment|Alignment]], and weapons with Matrix Traits add an effect based on it when they hit. Choosing a matrix is choosing a way to fight: Chaos hits harder, Frozen shrugs off melee and freezes attackers, Magic saves MRU, and Shade only starts working at rank 8, after which its traits heal you from the damage you deal. The {item:essentialcraft5:chaos_fork} and {item:essentialcraft5:frozen_mace} still need the matching matrix for their own effects ([[staffs/matrix_weapons]]).
How to use it

items: First right-click the projection once and let go. It is imprinted with your MRU matrix and becomes yours, and its tooltip names the owner. You can't use anyone else's.
Then find a safe spot, have food at hand, and hold right-click for 10 seconds.
A portal sound plays every 2 seconds. Nausea sets in with 5 seconds left, and blindness for the last 2.5 seconds.
The moment it finishes, the projection vanishes, your matrix changes, and a line in chat tells you so.

blocks.text: The cost

rows: Wither I, Weakness V, Slowness V, Mining Fatigue V and Hunger I, 38 seconds each
lasts about 100 seconds after you finish

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off once you have absorbed a matrix projection.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Let go halfway and it is wasted, and the nausea and blindness you already have stay. Do it with no monsters around, and eat right after.
To check your current matrix, look at the tooltip of a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_stone} bound to you ([[mru/soul_stone]]).

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:magical_digger}
entries.summary: An MRU pickaxe that mines anything
items: essentialcraft5:magical_digger

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make a {item:essentialcraft5:magical_digger}, a pickaxe that runs on MRU. It mines any block fast, blocks that normally need a proper tool still drop, and it never breaks. Unless you sneak, it also takes out the same blocks around the one you mine, which makes ore veins and tunnels much quicker work.
Prepare

One {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_pickaxe}, one {item:essentialcraft5:red_soul_matter}, two {item:essentialcraft5:earth_focus}es, two {item:essentialcraft5:fire_focus}es, two {item:minecraft:tnt} and one {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plate}, which can also be a pale or mithriline plate. The pickaxe is covered in [[gear/elemental_tools]] and the soul matter in [[storage/soul_storage]].

The four focuses take the longest. A focus needs fuel made from essences, the essences have to be drawn from elemental crystals you grow first, and fresh crystals are often low in elements ([[essence/fuel_and_focus]]). If you want a digger, start growing crystals early.

blocks.title: Save some for the main line
blocks.text: The main line still needs 4 {item:essentialcraft5:air_focus} for the [[wind/wind_tablet]] and 4 {item:essentialcraft5:fire_focus} for the [[demons/demonic_pentacle]]. Set those aside first and spend only the extras here.

blocks.title: Before crafting
blocks.text: Neither the enchantments on the elemental pickaxe nor the MRU stored in the {item:essentialcraft5:red_soul_matter} carry over to the digger, so spend that MRU before crafting. A new digger is empty. Charge it in the [[storage/charging_chamber]] before use.
How to use it
Hold it and mine as you would with any pickaxe.

items: It mines every block at speed 32 (diamond 8, netherite 9), so even obsidian takes just over two seconds. Everything drops as usual, and there is no need to switch tools.
Each block costs 9 MRU. If the storage items you carry, such as a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard}, can cover it between them, they pay; otherwise the digger pays from its own MRU.

Unless you sneak, mining a block also mines every block of the same kind in the 3×3×3 around it, at 9 MRU each, and stops when the MRU runs out. Sneaking mines only the block you hit, still for 9 MRU.
Blocks taken along count as mined by you. They drop items and experience as usual, and Fortune or Silk Touch on the digger applies to them.

rows: 32; only 1 when it holds less than 9 MRU itself
the same block within 3×3×3, at most 27 per swing

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have a digger. Charge it, mine some stone, and the stone around it goes too.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: When the digger itself holds less than 9 MRU, it slows right down to speed 1 and Efficiency stops helping. Stone takes over two seconds and obsidian over a minute. Blocks still drop and nothing is spent, but it stops taking blocks along, even if your storage items are full. Keep some MRU in the digger itself.
Fine print

items: Every block taken along counts as mined by you, so places you may not change, such as someone else's claim, the protected area around spawn or anywhere beyond the world border, are left alone and cost nothing.
It only takes blocks of the same kind as the one you mined. Mining stone takes only stone and leaves dirt and ores alone, and the area doesn't spread outward.

It has no durability and never breaks. At an enchanting table or anvil it takes pickaxe enchantments such as Efficiency, Fortune and Silk Touch, but not Unbreaking or Mending, which it has no use for anyway.

items.text: It is also an ingredient of the {item:essentialcraft5:ley_projector} ([[ley/ley_projector]]), and any MRU stored in it is used up by the craft.

blocks.text: The original research book subtitled it "A multitool?" and said it could stand in for "pretty much, any tool". In the original, mining a single block while sneaking was free, yet blocks you weren't allowed to mine still cost MRU.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:paving_wand}
entries.summary: Lay a whole floor in one click; the entry-level building wand
items: essentialcraft5:paving_wand
essentialcraft5:builder_module_range
essentialcraft5:builder_module_haste
essentialcraft5:builder_module_efficiency
essentialcraft5:builder_module_reach
essentialcraft5:builder_module_mix
essentialcraft5:builder_module_salvage

blocks.text: Goal (optional): craft a {item:essentialcraft5:paving_wand}. One right-click on the ground lays a whole floor, path or platform from the blocks you carry. It is the first tier of the building wand: it only places blocks into empty spots and never breaks anything.
Prepare

{item:essentialcraft5:world_interactor} ×1, {item:essentialcraft5:pale_plate} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:magic_fortified_plating} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_core} ×1 and {item:essentialcraft5:earth_focus} ×1. It comes out set to the Plane shape.

The World Interacting Device and fortified plating are covered in [[crafting/magician_crafts]], pale plates in [[alloys/pale]], the elemental core in [[elements/parts]] and the earth focus in [[essence/fuel_and_focus]].
How to use it

items: Sneak + right-click a block to <hl>select</hl> it; that is the block the wand lays. With a block in your off hand, the wand lays that one instead, with no need to select it.
Carry that block, then right-click the top of a block: the wand lays a layer above it, centred on that block, 5 × 5 by default. Right-click the air to lay it at your feet.
Hold the <hl>wand key</hl> ({keybind:key.essentialcraft5.builder_wand}, rebindable in the controls) and scroll to make the area larger or smaller.
Keep holding the wand and stay close while it works. Sneak + right-click the air to stop part-way; whatever is already laid stays.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You have the Paving Wand in your inventory. Point it at the ground and the area to be laid is marked out; right-click and the blocks spread outwards ring by ring from the spot you clicked.
Three shapes

The <hl>shape</hl> decides which blocks are covered. The Paving Wand has three, Two Points, Plane and Line, switched on the Area page of the Blueprint Table described below. The current shape and size appear in the wand's tooltip and below the crosshair while you hold it.

rows: Right-click two blocks to set the corners; the box between them is the selection. Right-click the air to start. When nothing is running, sneak + right-click the air clears the corners
Right-click the top or bottom of a block to lay a layer above or below it, centred on that block; right-click a side to lay it outwards from that side; right-click the air to lay it at your feet
Starts from the block just outside the face you click and runs the way you face; right-click the air to start at your feet

items: With Plane and Line a single right-click starts the work; no corners are needed. Sneak + right-click on a block still selects it, and sneak + right-click in the air still stops.

Hold the wand key and scroll to resize: a Plane grows or shrinks on both sides at once and becomes a square, a Line only changes length. Add sneak to change only the length of a Plane or only the width of a Line. While the wand key is held, scrolling does not change the hotbar slot.

A side can be at most {cfg:general.builder.paver.max_side} blocks, one job at most {cfg:general.builder.paver.max_volume} blocks, and the two corners at most {cfg:general.builder.paver.max_point_distance} blocks apart. Length runs the way you face and width spreads to both sides; with an even width the extra block goes to your right.
The area under the crosshair is marked out, and spots you lack the material or MRU for are shown in red.

The line below the crosshair shows the shape, size, how many blocks will be placed, how much material you carry and the MRU the job needs, with any shortfall in red. While building it shows progress and the time left, and it also says when the job is paused, queued or waiting for a second click.

blocks.text: The Blueprint Table

Hold the wand and tap the wand key to spread out the <hl>Blueprint Table</hl> across the screen; tap it again or press Esc to put it away. Shape, size, selected block and modules are all set here, and the blueprint on the left updates as you change them.

items: The top bar shows the wand's name, tier and stored MRU.

On the left is the blueprint, a top-down drawing of every block this job will touch, with blocks to be placed painted in that block's colour. Below it are the shape, size, number of blocks to place and the MRU the job needs, in red if you are short. While building, the blueprint fills in block by block.
Area page: pick the shape and mode; the Paving Wand only has Fill. Adjust the size with the plus and minus buttons below the blueprint, or hold the wand key and scroll.

Blocks page: lists every block you could build with, from your inventory and carried containers, sorted by count. Click one to make it the selected block. With a Mixing Module fitted, the mix table sits on the right.
Modules page: lists the fitted modules; each can be switched off or removed on its own, and removed modules go back to your inventory. Below them are the wand's current limits.

The bottom bar has Undo last and Stop at either end. Between them is the job that can be undone, with its shape, block count and how long ago it was placed, and the progress while building. When nothing can be undone the button is greyed out and the reason is shown.

While a job is running, paused or queued, every setting except Undo last and Stop is greyed out; stop first to change anything. Resizing by holding the wand key and scrolling also needs the job stopped.
While the Blueprint Table is open, the line below the crosshair is hidden.

blocks.text: Materials and MRU

items: It only uses items that aren't renamed and hold nothing: your inventory first, then your off hand.

items.text: When those run short it takes from containers you carry, meaning bag-like items with their own slots, in your inventory, off hand, armor or accessory slots. Stacked containers and containers inside containers are left alone, and nothing is taken from carried containers while another container screen is open.
Material that a container's own rules won't let out is not counted as carried, nor when checking whether you have enough before starting.

items: The wand holds 5,000 MRU of its own and comes out empty, so charge it in the [[storage/charging_chamber]]. It draws from the storage items you carry first ([[storage/soul_storage]]) and only then from itself.
Each block placed costs 25 MRU; spots that already hold a block and skipped spots cost nothing. Filling the largest area takes {cfg:general.builder.paver.max_volume|mul:25} MRU.

items.text: When materials or MRU run out it <hl>pauses</hl> for {cfg:general.builder.material_pause_seconds} seconds and carries on if you top up in time; otherwise it stops and keeps what is already laid.

items: For a very large job, or when you clearly lack the materials or MRU, the first right-click only warns you. Right-click again within 3 seconds to start that same job.

blocks.text: Undo

items: Hold the wand key and right-click, or click Undo last on the Blueprint Table, to undo the last placement: the blocks are taken back and the material is refunded one for one. MRU is not refunded.
Only the most recent placement can be undone, within {cfg:general.builder.undo_window_seconds} seconds, in the same dimension, and no farther from the area than the wand's work range.
Spots that have since been mined, replaced with another block, grown, or had a slab completed into a double slab are left alone and refund nothing.
Undo claims blocks by type: if a spot later holds the same kind of block again, whoever placed it and however it got there, it is taken back and refunded too.
If an undo is interrupted, the rest stays on record and can be undone later. The record is cleared when you log out.

blocks.text: Modules

The Paving Wand has 2 module slots. Put the wand and one module in a crafting grid with nothing else, and the result is the wand with that module fitted. Each kind of module fits only once; modules are removed on the Modules page of the Blueprint Table.

rows: Work range +{cfg:general.builder.modules.reach.reach_bonus} blocks; a Plane can be aimed as far as the work range
Lays up to {cfg:general.builder.modules.mix.max_kinds} kinds of blocks mixed in set proportions

items: With a Reach Module, the area is still marked out when the crosshair is on a distant block, and a right-click starts the work there.

With a Mixing Module, set up the mix table on the Blocks page of the Blueprint Table: give each block a weight from 1 to 9, and higher weights are laid more often. When one kind runs out, the others fill in.
The {item:essentialcraft5:builder_module_salvage} only fits a Magical Building Wand, not the Paving Wand.

blocks.text: Recipes and full details for every module are in [[void_machines/builder_module]].

items: essentialcraft5:builder_module_range
essentialcraft5:builder_module_haste
essentialcraft5:builder_module_efficiency
essentialcraft5:builder_module_reach
essentialcraft5:builder_module_mix

blocks.text: Upgrading to tier 2

Once you have materials from Hoanna, the Paving Wand can be upgraded into the tier 2 [[void_machines/magical_builder|Magical Building Wand]]: lay out the Magical Building Wand recipe with the Paving Wand in place of one of the whitelist filters. Stored MRU, the selected block and fitted modules are kept, and the result is in Fill mode.

blocks.caption: Either the upper or the lower filter can be replaced

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Blocks in someone else's claim are left alone and cost nothing, but once {cfg:general.builder.denied_limit} have been refused the wand stops, so keep clear of other people's claims. Also, some blocks do something extra when placed by hand, such as using up two items or storing extra data. The wand only places the block itself, so such blocks may not turn out the same as hand-placed ones.
Fine print

items: Blocks face the way they would if you placed them by hand from where you stand, so stairs and the like follow the direction you face. Slabs go in as bottom halves, candles and sea pickles as one, and crops start freshly planted.

If the new block can't stay in a spot, such as a flower on stone or kelp out of water, or someone is standing there, the spot is left untouched and costs nothing. The message at the end says how many spots were skipped.
Sand, gravel and other falling blocks are skipped where there is nothing under them, so no falling blocks are spawned.

It stops if you change what's in your hand, walk out of work range or change dimension. Each player works one area at a time. Starting another while one runs queues it, and if too many players are building at once you wait your turn; it starts by itself.
In Creative mode it costs no MRU or materials.
The marked-out area, the line below the crosshair and the size that asks for a second click can all be changed in the mod's client settings.

blocks.text: Further reading: to remove or replace blocks, raise walls or cover uneven ground, you need the tier 2 [[void_machines/magical_builder|Magical Building Wand]].

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe} and {item:essentialcraft5:essential_axe}
entries.summary: Mine a 3×3 face, fell a whole tree
items: essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe
essentialcraft5:essential_axe

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make an {item:essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe} or an {item:essentialcraft5:essential_axe}. Both run on MRU and never break. The pickaxe takes out the 3×3 on the face you mine, and when the axe chops one log the whole tree comes down.
Prepare

The pickaxe needs an {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_pickaxe} and the axe an {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_axe} ([[gear/elemental_tools]]). Each also takes two {item:essentialcraft5:mithriline_plate}s, one {item:essentialcraft5:wind_gem}, two {item:essentialcraft5:mru_resonating_crystal}s and one {item:essentialcraft5:dark_soul_matter}. The wind crystal has to wait for Chapter 13 ([[wind/wind_gem]]).

blocks.title: Before crafting
blocks.text: Neither the enchantments on the elemental tool nor the MRU stored in the {item:essentialcraft5:dark_soul_matter} carry over, so spend that MRU before crafting. A fresh pickaxe or axe is empty; charge it in the [[storage/charging_chamber]] before use.
How to use it
Hold it and mine as you would with an ordinary pickaxe or axe.

items: While it holds enough MRU of its own for one block, the pickaxe mines stone and ores, and the axe cuts wood, at speed 12, against 9 for netherite tools. Below that it drops to speed 1.

The {item:essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe} spends {cfg:general.essential_tools.mru_per_block} MRU per block and the {item:essentialcraft5:essential_axe} {cfg:general.essential_tools.mru_per_log} MRU per block, the one you hit included. The storage items you carry pay when together they can cover it, otherwise the tool pays from its own MRU, and when neither can pay for the next block, nothing more is taken along. On blocks the tool isn't meant for, such as dirt for the pickaxe or stone for the axe, it works like a plain tool, spending nothing and taking nothing along.
The pickaxe also mines the 3×3 centered on the block, on the face you hit. A wall gives an upright 3×3, and a floor or ceiling a flat one.

When the axe chops a log or stem, every connected log of the same kind falls one after another over a few ticks, and the drops all land where you chopped. The leaves stay put and fall away on their own later.
Sneak to mine or chop only the block you hit. It still costs that one block.
Blocks taken along count as mined by you. They drop items and experience as usual, and Fortune or Silk Touch on the tool applies to them.

rows: 12; only 1 while it holds less than one block's worth itself
the 3×3 on the face you hit, at most 8 extra blocks

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have either tool. Charge the pickaxe and mine one block of a stone wall, and the 8 blocks around it go too.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The axe only brings down natural trees. The connected logs need at least {cfg:general.essential_tools.leaves_required} leaves that grew there on their own, or nether wart and warped wart blocks for huge fungi. Log houses and pillars have none, and leaves you placed yourself don't count, so there the axe cuts only the log you hit.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The axe brings down every connected log of the same kind, log houses and pillars included. Look before you chop.
Fine print

items: When taking blocks along, the pickaxe leaves these alone: blocks with a block entity, such as chests, furnaces, spawners and machines, unbreakable blocks such as bedrock, blocks a pickaxe isn't meant for, and blocks much harder than the one you hit. The others may be at most {cfg:general.essential_tools.hardness_margin} harder than the center, so mining stone never takes obsidian with it.
A few blocks are never taken along and only break when they are the block you hit, so rare blocks that drop nothing aren't destroyed by accident.

The axe searches only upward and on the same level, never below the log you chop. It reaches at most {cfg:general.essential_tools.felling_radius} blocks sideways and {cfg:general.essential_tools.felling_height} blocks up, takes only logs of the same kind as the one you chopped, and cuts the nearest first.
While a tree is still coming down, chopping another log cuts just that log. If you switch what is in your main hand, change dimension or die halfway, the rest stays standing.
Blocks in places you may not change, such as someone else's claim, the protected area around spawn or beyond the world border, are left alone and cost nothing.

Neither tool has durability. They take Efficiency, Fortune and Silk Touch but not Unbreaking or Mending. The {item:essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe} gets drops from every block a netherite pickaxe can. The axe still strips logs with right-click.
In Creative mode both mine a single block and spend nothing.

The [[gear/magical_digger]] takes the same kind of block within 3×3×3, which suits ore veins. The {item:essentialcraft5:essential_pickaxe} mines one face whatever the stone, which makes it the better tool for tunnels and clearing ground.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem}
entries.summary: Diamonds and emeralds for this mod's recipes
items: essentialcraft5:pale_gem

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make a few {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem}s in the {item:essentialcraft5:radiating_chamber}. You can only start once you have a {item:essentialcraft5:pale_block} from Chapter 12.

Most recipes in this mod that ask for a diamond or an emerald take a pale gem instead. The {item:essentialcraft5:diamond_plate}, {item:essentialcraft5:emerald_plate}, {item:essentialcraft5:mru_resonating_crystal}, {item:essentialcraft5:matrix_link}, {item:essentialcraft5:soul_sphere}, {item:essentialcraft5:red_soul_matter}, {item:essentialcraft5:emerald_heart} and {item:essentialcraft5:mru_mover_t2} all accept it.

One diamond becomes four pale gems. A resonating crystal normally takes a diamond and an emerald; with pale gems, one diamond covers two crystals. Later chapters use a lot of resonating crystals, so the swap pays off whenever diamonds are scarce.
You need: one {item:essentialcraft5:pale_block} ([[pentacle/pale_block]]) and one diamond or emerald. Each batch costs 30,000 MRU and gives four.
It also works as a lens for the {item:essentialcraft5:ley_projector}. Put one in the lens slot and projected ores drop as with Fortune I, without using up the gem ([[ley/ley_lens]]).

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off once you have a pale gem.

blocks.title: Where it does not count
blocks.text: Pale gems only stand in within this mod's recipes. The following don't take them.

items: Vanilla recipes and other mods' recipes.
Making pale gems itself needs a real diamond or emerald, not another pale gem.
Swapping diamonds and emeralds in the {item:essentialcraft5:mithriline_furnace}, and imbuing a {item:essentialcraft5:wind_gem}, only accept the real thing.

The diamond slot in the middle of the {item:essentialcraft5:crystal_former}'s top row, and the two rituals where you throw a diamond or an emerald onto an emerald block, which are the diamond ritual in [[start/mrucu]] and the one in [[mru/soul_stone]].

blocks.text: In the original mod a pale gem counted as a diamond or an emerald in every mod's recipes, even as rubies and sapphires. It could be made into more pale gems, or swapped back for real diamonds in the Mithriline Furnace, so one diamond snowballed into eight.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:ley_detector}
entries.summary: Outlines nearby ores, for your eyes only
items: essentialcraft5:ley_detector

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make a {item:essentialcraft5:ley_detector}. Right-click and the ores near you get a glowing outline you can see through stone, so you can dig straight to them instead of tunneling blind.
Prepare

Four {item:essentialcraft5:mithriline_ingot}s ([[mithriline/mithriline_ingot]]), one {item:essentialcraft5:magical_screen}, two {item:essentialcraft5:earth_focus}es ([[essence/fuel_and_focus]]), one {item:essentialcraft5:magic_monocle} ([[gear/magic_monocle]]) and one {item:minecraft:compass}.
A fresh detector holds no MRU, so charge it in the [[storage/charging_chamber]] first.
How to use it

items: Hold it and right-click. Each scan costs {cfg:general.ley_detector.mru_per_scan} MRU, paid by the storage items you carry (such as a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard}) when they can cover it, otherwise by the detector itself.
Every ore within {cfg:general.ley_detector.radius} blocks of the block you stand on gets an outline. If there are too many, only the nearest ones do.
The outlines stay for a while and fade out over the last 3 seconds.
Sneak and right-click to cycle through "all ores", "valuable ores only" and "MRUCUs". Switching costs nothing.

rows: diamond, emerald, gold, ancient debris and mithriline
every other ore, including ores from other mods

blocks.text: In "valuable ores only" mode, only the gold ones are outlined.

In "MRUCUs" mode no ores are outlined. Instead it points toward the nearest MRUCU holding {cfg:general.mobs.mru_golem.detector_min_mru} MRU or more within {cfg:general.mobs.mru_golem.detector_radius} blocks, which is usually the one in an ancient ruin ([[bestiary/mru_golem]]). It only searches chunks that are already loaded.

A right-click costs {cfg:general.ley_detector.mru_per_scan} MRU and starts the same cooldown as an ore scan. The action bar shows which way the MRUCU is, how far away horizontally, how many blocks up or down, and how much MRU it holds, and a short line of cyan specks points that way in front of you. Only you can see them. If no suitable MRUCU is nearby it says so, and the MRU is still spent.

rows: {cfg:general.ley_detector.radius} blocks from you in every direction

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have a detector. Charge it, right-click in a mine, and the ores nearby light up.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The outlines show on your screen only; people next to you can't see them. A scan is centered where you stood when you right-clicked, and the outlines don't follow you, so scan again once you've moved on.
Fine print

items: When an outlined block is mined or replaced, its outline disappears at once.
A new scan replaces the old outlines. Changing dimension or leaving the game clears them.
During the cooldown right-clicking does nothing, and the item icon shows the cooldown overlay.
A scan takes a few ticks, and the new outlines appear only once it's done.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:homeward_compass}
entries.summary: Set a home point and channel back to it
items: essentialcraft5:homeward_compass

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make a {item:essentialcraft5:homeward_compass}. Set a home point at your base, and from then on, wherever you are, you can hold right-click for a few seconds and be sent back.
Prepare

Four {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_ender_scale_alloy}s ([[storage/upgrades]]), one {item:essentialcraft5:wind_gem} ([[wind/wind_gem]]), two {item:minecraft:ender_eye}s, one {item:essentialcraft5:dark_soul_matter} ([[storage/soul_storage]]) and one {item:minecraft:compass}.
How to use it

items: Sneak and right-click a block to make it your home point. You arrive standing on top of it, so pick a floor block with open space above. You can set a new one at any time.
To go back, hold right-click and stand still. The compass channels for {cfg:general.homeward_compass.channel_ticks|sec} while purple portal particles drift around you.
When the channel completes you're sent to your home point. MRU is paid only then, all of it from storage items you carry; the compass holds none itself.

blocks.text: Moving more than {cfg:general.homeward_compass.move_tolerance} blocks, getting hurt or letting go of the button breaks the channel. That costs nothing and starts no cooldown, so just hold right-click again.
When it won't start
In these cases right-clicking doesn't start a channel, and the reason appears above your hotbar.

items: You were hit by a mob or another player within the last {cfg:general.homeward_compass.combat_lock_ticks|sec}.
You have {lang:effect.essentialcraft5.anchored} on you, or you're riding something.
The compass is still cooling down.
The storage items you carry can't cover the trip.

rows: {cfg:general.homeward_compass.base_mru} MRU plus {cfg:general.homeward_compass.mru_per_block} MRU per block, at most {cfg:general.homeward_compass.max_mru_same_dimension} MRU

blocks.text: Distance is the straight horizontal line from where you stand to the home point, and height doesn't count. The item tooltip shows what the trip costs from where you are now.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: This step is checked off as soon as you have a compass. Set a home point, walk some way off, hold right-click, and a few seconds later you're back on that floor block.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: If the landing spot is no good when the channel completes, you don't go. Something may block the space above the home point, the floor block may be gone, or there may be lava, fire or something else harmful there. The compass tells you why, and the trip costs nothing and starts no cooldown.
Fine print

items.text: The compass can't take you into Hoanna from another dimension. The only way in is through the [[hoanna/open_gate|Gate to Hoanna]]. A home point set inside Hoanna still works while you're in Hoanna.
You can use the compass to get back from Hoanna. For the other ways home, see [[hoanna/way_home]].
The compass only takes you to a home point in the same dimension.

items: If {lang:effect.essentialcraft5.anchored} lands on you mid-channel, the trip breaks off too, again at no cost.
The cooldown survives leaving and rejoining the game. It's cleared only when you die.
You can't set a home point anywhere you aren't allowed to build, such as someone else's claim or the protected area around spawn. If a claim later covers your home point, you can't land there either.
If your home point is far away, the compass waits up to 2 seconds for that area to load after the channel completes. Stay put meanwhile.
